---
title: "Decoder"
description: "A model component that transforms representations into an output or generated sequence."
term: "Decoder"
letter: "D"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

A decoder turns an internal representation into an output. Depending on
the architecture, it might reconstruct an image, generate text, or map a
compressed representation into another format.

## Technical explanation

The term has architecture-specific meanings. In an encoder-decoder model,
the decoder consumes an encoded representation and produces outputs.
Transformer decoders may use causal self-attention for autoregressive
generation, while other decoders use cross-attention to incorporate
encoder outputs. Some models are decoder-only and generate from prior
tokens without a separate encoder.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Knowing what a model's decoder does helps engineers understand generation,
sequence alignment, conditioning, and inference costs. The term should be
interpreted in the context of a particular architecture.

## How it works

A decoder receives latent features, encoder states, previous output
tokens, or a combination of them. Learned layers transform this context
into the next representation or output. In autoregressive models, the
decoder repeats next-token prediction until a stopping condition is met.

## Practical example

An image autoencoder uses an encoder to create a compact representation
and a decoder to reconstruct an image from it.

## Common misconceptions

- A decoder does not always mean the generation component of a language
  model.
- Not every decoder has an encoder paired with it.
- Decoder architecture alone does not determine output quality.
